name: Royal Crescent

refs.title: Nos. 1-30, ROYAL CRESCENT, Non Civil Parish - 1394736 | Historic England
refs.note: Grade I. One entry covers all thirty houses, which is why this record can quote the crescent as a whole rather than one range of it.

survey.prepared: The entry's own Details header prints the listing date 12/06/50. The Overview block was not returned by the extract.

quotes.text: ROYAL CRESCENT 656-1/29/1427 Nos.1-30 (Consec) Formerly Listed as: ROYAL CRESCENT Nos 1-7 (consec). No.8. Nos 9-30 (consec) 12/06/50 GV I Thirty houses, concave semi-elliptical crescent. 1767-1775 with C20 alterations. By John Wood the Younger.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1394736, Details, entry header and opening sentence

quotes.text: MATERIALS: Even and finely cut limestone ashlar; double pitched slate mansard roofs (originally stone-tiled) with moulded stacks to coped party walls.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1394736, Details, MATERIALS paragraph

quotes.text: EXTERIOR: A crescent some 500ft (152m.) long and nearly 50ft (15m.) tall, fronted with a procession of 114 engaged giant Ionic columns, each some 20ft (6m.) tall; columns are placed singly between bays apart from the centremost bay, which is flanked with pairs; further pairs to the corners of the end houses.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1394736, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: All houses comprise three storeys with attics and basements, and mostly with three-window fronts: Nos 14-17, to centre, have four-window fronts.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1394736, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: Continuous returned balustraded parapet, modillion cornice and frieze supported by giant order of 114 Roman Ionic engaged columns that rise from the plain ground floor plinth with platband.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1394736, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: Unadorned rectangular door and window openings; mainly six/six-pane sash windows, many restored in recent years but some still retain Victorian plate glass intrusions; some with balconettes and blind boxes. Dormer windows to attics, generally three per front.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1394736, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

measurements.name: facade_length_ft
measurements.note: The entry's own approximation, printed in both units. It is the length of the whole crescent of thirty houses, not of one house.

measurements.name: facade_height_ft
measurements.note: The entry says 'nearly 50ft', so 50 is an upper bound the entry states rather than a measured height. Over three storeys with attics and basements.

measurements.name: column_count
measurements.as_printed: a procession of 114 engaged giant Ionic columns

measurements.name: column_height_ft
measurements.note: The giant order runs through the first and second floors above a plain ground-floor plinth, so this is not a storey height.

measurements.name: storey_count
measurements.as_printed: All houses comprise three storeys with attics and basements
measurements.note: Three main storeys, with the attic and basement named separately.

measurements.name: centre_house_bay_count
measurements.as_printed: Nos 14-17, to centre, have four-window fronts

measurements.name: dormer_count_per_house
measurements.as_printed: Dormer windows to attics, generally three per front
measurements.note: 'Generally' is the entry's word; it is a typical figure and not a count of every front.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. A group record shared by two nodes at one location string. This entry is the richest in the cluster for dimensions: it states the crescent's length, its height, the number of columns and the height of a column, in feet and metres alike. The height and length are the entry's own approximations ('some', 'nearly') and are carried as such.
